why: This is the classic interval merge: once intervals are sorted by start, any overlap can only be with the interval you are currently building, so one left-to-right sweep merges everything.
hints: If the intervals were sorted by start, which earlier intervals could the next one overlap?

After sorting, the next interval overlaps the running merged interval exactly when its start is at most the running end (closed intervals). Then extend the end to max(end, new end); otherwise close it and start a new one.
Sort by start (O(n log n)), then a single sweep holding the current merged interval; output is built in order.
pitfalls: Touching endpoints like [1,4] and [4,5] count as overlapping because the intervals are closed.
A contained interval like [1,10] then [2,3] must not shrink the end: use max.
